procedure: Open a fresh tab for each primary service and scan every frozen human/AI pair once in ordered_pairs order.
Before every submit, bind the visible full text to its frozen SHA-256.
Accept a repeat only after a first-scan marker, visible loading/disabled state, changed result identifier, or changed result text proves a new transition.
Do not write, alter, or scan an edit variant during this scout.
Classify each pair/service baseline with the frozen usable-cell rule.
If either service cell is usable for a pair, repeat the unchanged human and AI texts in both primary services until n=3; otherwise keep n=1.
Select only cross-family windows for a later edit experiment; single-family windows remain diagnostics.

usable_cell_rule.cell_pass: terminal complete and all numeric thresholds pass on the first scan in the same service

selection_rule.single_family_window: exactly one primary service cell passes
selection_rule.selected_pairs: first two cross_family_window pairs in ordered_pairs order
selection_rule.diagnostic_pairs: all single_family_window pairs in ordered_pairs order
selection_rule.no_cross_family_window: stop without edit variants and report that the current accessible detector pair cannot jointly resolve minimal effects on this frozen corpus

interpretation_limits: This is detector-based calibration selection and therefore cannot support a detector-generalization or authorship claim.
A score at 0 or 100 is a floor/ceiling observation and cannot rank local edits.
A human false positive is evidence about detector validity on that genre; the human control is never edited.
An AI-polish row is a measurement target, not an endorsed upstream rewriting method.
A single-family window cannot launch an edit experiment under this preregistration.
Any later edit experiment requires a new frozen preregistration with exact operations, fidelity, source-as-reference style, and English-level envelopes.
